title: Lie Groups And Lie Algebras
notes: Open the lecture by stressing the chapter's central tension: a Lie group is a global manifold with multiplication, while its Lie algebra is a first-order object at the identity. The source span 98-154 is best taught as a sequence of bridges from local analytic data to global topology.

title: Chapter Roadmap
notes: Use the roadmap as a dependency graph, not a table of contents. The exponential map creates one-parameter subgroups; brackets control local multiplication; subgroups and cosets add topology; the adjoint action exposes semisimple structure; invariant forms return the algebra to differential geometry.

title: Analytic Groups Have Tangent Algebra
notes: Emphasize that the Lie algebra is not a separate object chosen after the fact. Left-invariant vector fields convert tangent vectors at the identity into global infinitesimal motions, and the commutator of those fields gives the bracket that remembers the group law to second order.

title: Exponential Map As Motion
notes: The SE(2) model makes the exponential map concrete. A vector with angular and translational parts integrates to a rigid motion path. Near the identity this gives useful coordinates, while the one-parameter subgroup identity gives the algebraic reason the construction belongs to Lie theory.

title: Local Law And The Bracket
notes: The Baker-Campbell-Hausdorff picture should be presented as a local statement. The linear terms add tangent vectors, the first correction is the bracket, and higher terms encode iterated commutators. This is where noncommutativity first becomes visible in coordinates near the identity.

title: PBW Turns Brackets Into Normal Forms
notes: Introduce the universal enveloping algebra as an accounting device. It embeds Lie bracket information into an associative algebra by forcing XY minus YX to equal the bracket. The Heisenberg example is small enough that students can see a word being rewritten into PBW order.

title: Subalgebras Integrate, But Images Need Not Close
notes: This is the global warning after the local theory. A subalgebra integrates to a connected immersed subgroup, but the image can wind densely in a compact ambient group. The torus line with irrational slope is the cleanest way to separate algebraic integration from closed embedded subgroup structure.

title: Cosets Convert Symmetry Into Space
notes: Frame a homogeneous space as the record of where a base point can be moved. The stabilizer H captures the ambiguity in choosing a group element, so the quotient G/H becomes the geometric object. SO(3)/SO(2) equals the sphere because only the image of the north pole matters.

title: Transformation Groups Produce Fundamental Fields
notes: Connect actions back to calculus on manifolds. Every Lie algebra vector differentiates an action curve through each point, producing a fundamental vector field. Isotropy kills the field at the base point, while directions transverse to isotropy become tangent directions on the orbit.

title: Adjoint Action Differentiates Conjugation
notes: The adjoint representation measures how the group moves its own infinitesimal directions. In sl(2), conjugation by exp(tH) expands the E direction and contracts the F direction. The identity Ad(exp X) equals exp(ad X) is a precise bridge from group conjugation to the bracket.

title: Killing Form Detects Semisimplicity
notes: Present the Killing form as a trace measurement of how strongly the algebra acts on itself. Nondegeneracy is the semisimple diagnostic. Over the real numbers, the signature matters: sl(2,R) is semisimple but indefinite, while a compact semisimple real form has negative definite Killing form.

title: Invariant Forms Store Structure Constants
notes: Bring the chapter back to differential forms. A left-invariant coframe turns bracket constants into exterior derivative equations. In the Heisenberg group, the central coordinate records swept area, and d omega3 equals minus omega1 wedge omega2, so the algebra is visible in the calculus of forms.

title: Semisimple Groups And Invariant Metrics
notes: Use this synthesis slide to connect algebraic diagnostics to geometry. Semisimplicity removes solvable ideals, the Killing form supplies canonical bilinear data, and invariant forms or metrics move that data around the group. Compactness changes the signature, not the need for invariance.

title: Local-Global Failure Modes
notes: Slow down on this slide because it prevents overgeneralization. Exponential coordinates, subgroup integration, and quotient construction are powerful, but each has a hypothesis boundary. The errors come from confusing local diffeomorphisms with global parametrizations, immersed subgroups with closed subgroups, or orbit sets with manifolds.

title: Recap: From Identity To Geometry
notes: Close by tracing the loop once more. The identity tangent space gives the Lie algebra; the exponential and BCH formula explain local multiplication; subgroups, cosets, and actions build spaces; the adjoint and Killing forms reveal structure; Maurer-Cartan equations translate the algebra back into differential geometry.
